CHIEF COMPLAINT
Lung nodule found on imaging during workup for cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Kyle is a patient with a three-month history of cough that began after loading hay while managing horses. He subsequently developed a cold which prompted him to see his primary care physician. PCP diagnosed bronchitis and ordered a chest X-ray to rule out pneumonia. The chest X-ray revealed a lung nodule. A subsequent CT scan confirmed the finding, and the patient was referred to pulmonology. The patient reports the cough has since resolved. He denies current pain, shortness of breath, or fever. He reports being very active with biking and exercises regularly, which typically keeps him in good health.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies shortness of breath, chest pain, or fever. Cough has resolved. No respiratory symptoms at present.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis - currently fair control with active lifestyle management.

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly for rheumatoid arthritis.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with history of breast cancer, currently doing well. No family history of lung cancer or other malignancies. No family history of lung infections or pneumonia.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Former smoker, quit approximately 7 years ago. Lives with family who supported smoking cessation. Enjoys biking and regular exercise. Manages horses and performs hay loading activities.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: BP 124/76, HR 70, RR 16, O2 saturation 98% on room air, afebrile.
Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally on auscultation.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no clicks, rubs, or murmurs, no extra beats appreciated.
Extremities: Skin pink, warm, and dry. No edema to lower extremities. Mild swelling of knuckles on third digits bilaterally consistent with rheumatoid arthritis. Pulses intact in all extremities with brisk capillary refill.

RESULTS
Chest CT: Solitary 2 cm smooth nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe. No evidence of emphysematous disease.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right upper lobe lung nodule, incidentally found. Plan to proceed with pulmonary function tests as baseline. PET CT ordered to assess metabolic activity of nodule to help determine if malignant versus inflammatory etiology. Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) recommended for nodule removal with small portion of lung tissue. Procedure will involve three small incisions on right chest wall under general anesthesia, expected duration approximately 90 minutes. Patient will be admitted overnight with chest tube placement, anticipated removal at bedside the following day prior to discharge. Rheumatoid arthritis to continue management with rheumatologist and current medication therapy.
